string.text: JitProfiler samples the running Lua stack on the engine timer and names the mod behind each hot script. These are the capture defaults. The in-game panel and the console commands both use them, and a console argument overrides the matching value for a single capture.
How often the CPU sampler fires. Lower samples more often and costs a little more per second; higher is cheaper and coarser. A console argument to start_cpu overrides this for that capture.

How many stack frames each sample records. Deeper traces reach further toward the root and fill the callers and callees view, at a higher cost per sample. Applies to both the CPU and the allocation capture.
How many rows each ranked view prints in the text report. The in-game panel lists every row regardless of this value.
During an allocation capture the profiler writes a numbered snapshot and keeps going once its table reaches this fraction of capacity, so a long session never overflows the table.

Stops a running capture on its own after this many seconds and writes the report. Zero leaves the capture running until you stop it. A safety limit worth setting for the allocation profile, which holds the JIT off for the whole capture.
Fold the vanilla baseline in reports
Drops the anomaly rows from the owned views in the text report, leaving mod cost. The console set_fold_anomaly overrides this for the session.
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first; otherwise they override the reset on the next Accept.
Restore all JitProfiler MCM settings to their defaults.
